items.title: MIT Shows An AI Can Edit Another Model's Weights And Lift Math Score To 48.1%
items.summary: MIT researchers are using AI to edit neural network weights directly, bypassing traditional training methods. This breakthrough, demonstrated by GPT-6 Astra, allows researchers to identify and fix specific internal errors within models by modifying raw weights rather than relying on forward path execution. By adjusting just 131,072 of the 800 million weights in the Qwen 3.5 model, the team achieved a significant jump in math performance, moving from 7.9% to 48.1% accuracy. This approach to ai news suggests a future where models can perform self-directed surgery to debug their own reasoning. While the technique shows promise, the team notes that complex errors in models like Gemma 3 remain a hurdle. This development in ai marks a shift in how we interact with machine intelligence, moving closer to systems that can autonomously optimize their own architecture. items.title: OpenAI Signs Four Abu Dhabi Deals Across Energy, Government And Investment

This deal marks a significant geopolitical shift, signaling that the era of centralized Silicon Valley cloud computing is evolving. items.title: The Silent Failure in Every Multi-Agent System (with Vijoy Pandey)
items.summary: #multiagentsystems #agentobservability #quantumnetworking In Episode #1041, Dr. Vijoy Pandey (SVP and General Manager of Outshift, Cisco's incubation engine) returns for a third visit to explain why multi-agent systems fail without anyone noticing. Agents from different vendors, clouds and organisations can now exchange perfectly valid messages, but connection is not cognition: they do not agree on what those messages mean. Vijoy's team analyzed multi-agent sessions from its own production deployments and from public traces, and found a cognitive failure in every single one. In this episode, he lays out the kinds of failure he sees and how fast they compound, introduces the open-source observability platform and protocols Outshift has shipped to catch and correct drift mid-task, details a record-breaking quantum network running on real New York City fiber, and explains why probabilistic AI software running on deterministic hardware is a mismatch worth fixing. items.title: AI Could Take Your Job Before You Even Apply For It
items.summary: According to the Fed, companies are slowing hiring after investing in AI. This may seem obvious, but the headlines mostly focus on layoffs. Hiring slowdowns rarely make the news. The October Beige Book has specific examples. A Dallas accounting firm is holding off on entry-level contracts. IT contacts in Minneapolis told the Fed that AI is “dampening the creation of new jobs.” That matters because a slowdown like this is invisible. There’s no severance announcement or headline attached to it. The people who feel it first are the ones still trying to get hired.
